You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task notes

## task-d394a1b8 (2026-09-29)
Demo showed a 19x14 grid split into upper 9x14 sparse noise, a separator row, and lower 9x14 binary-pattern panel. Output was the lower panel with color substitution: input 8 -> output 1, input 1 -> output 3. Thus isolate the content panel, preserve its dimensions/positions, and recolor its two symbols (the sparse foreground symbol maps to 3; dominant background maps to 1).

Test was 17x29 with left panel (cols 0-13), divider col14=0, right panel (cols15-28). Right panel is predominantly 5 with sparse 9s. Likely content panel substitution: 5->1 and 9->3, yielding 17x14. Multiple submissions were wrong because I manually transcribed sparse 9 locations inaccurately and kept submitting nearly identical grids; next time transcribe systematically or use a small script to extract/recolor the correct subgrid. I did not discover whether left panel provides any needed mask/role clue. Do not trust the mistaken submitted matrices as solutions.

## task-d0c248c0 (2026-09-29)
Task rule: a grid contains multiple solid rectangular color regions plus scattered noise cells (often color 4). Remove noise by completing each rectangular region to its full bounding rectangle, and set all other cells back to the dominant/background color (8 in this test). Rectangles may have one or more marker/noise cells embedded that should be replaced by region's color; also noise can be adjacent to/overlap the rectangle edge, so infer full rectangle boundary from consistent sides and color. In test solved output, preserve these rectangles (coordinates 0-indexed):
- color 6: rows 0-1, cols 10-14 (5x2)
- color 7: rows 1-2, cols 0-2 (3x2)
- color 0: rows 4-6, cols 7-12 (6x3)
- color 0: rows 8-11, cols 4-9 (6x4)
- color 7: rows 13-15, cols 4-7 (4x3)
- color 9: rows 15-18, cols 10-14 (5x4)
- color 6: rows 20-24, cols 1-6 (6x5)
- color 7: rows 21-25, cols 10-14 (5x5)
- color 9: rows 26-28, cols 1-3 (3x3)
Everything else is background 8. Demo pairs show exactly this denoising/completion operation: e.g. rectangular blocks with marker values 2/4/other intrusions restored to the block's uniform color; unrelated speckle cells removed to background. Key caution: preserve embedded region pixels by filling to shape's color, not deleting them; and fill missing rectangle edge cells where isolated noise lies. The successful test required restoring 4 at row0,col14 to 6, which was missed in earlier attempts. One demo request was useful to identify rule; avoid speculative submissions before mapping every rectangle's bounding box.
